subject: Stormridge production: sudden p99 latency & 5xx surge after v3.2 quant change
messages:
From: Olivia Hart <olivia.hart@stormridge.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Guerrero <alex.guerrero@stormridge.ai>
Date: 2026-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production alert — spike in p99 latency and 5xx after v3.2 quant swap

Hi Priya,

We're seeing a sharp rise in p99 latency (from ~280ms to ~1.6s) and an accompanying increase in 5xx responses across our inference path starting at ~08:40 PT this morning. This began right after our automated rollout of model v3.2 with the new quantization profile that Redwood suggested last week.

Symptoms:
- p50 unchanged, p95 up slightly, p99 jumped to ~1.6s
- 5xx rate rose to 0.9% (baseline ~0.02%)
- Throughput briefly dipped during the spike, then recovered but latency stayed high

We rolled back the model on our side but the metrics didn't fully recover until we disabled the new qprofile at ~09:00 (partial). We're attaching a short sample of 5xx logs and p99 trend PNG. Can you confirm whether any runtime-side kernel changes / scheduler changes were pushed during your V3.2 rollout window? This is causing customer-facing errors and our CS teams are getting escalations.

We need:
1) Immediate timeline and remediation plan from Redwood.
2) A determination if this is a quant-profile-induced decode stall or runtime OOM pattern.
3) Any recommended short-term mitigations while we coordinate rollback.

Thanks — really need fast triage.

Olivia

Subject: RE: Production alert — spike in p99 latency and 5xx after v3.2 quant swap

Priya / team — looking into this now. Early findings from a quick triage (10:40 PT):
- We see a correlation between the v3.2 qprofile activation and increased decode loop duration on several GPU hosts (NVIDIA A10G).
- A subset of requests show repeated kernel retries and short-lived memory spikes; these patterns can surface as 502/503 when the inference worker restarts or fails fast.
- No control-plane change was deployed from our side during the customer's rollout window. The change appears tied to the quant profile's kernel selection path for this model family (decoder-heavy sequences).

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Hot rollback of qprofile for Stormridge back to the previous quantization settings (fastest, safe).
2) If rollback isn't acceptable, push a runtime guard that limits concurrency on the affected hosts + per-request fallback to a CPU-safe decoder (slower but stable).

I'll pull the serving traces for the request-ids once Olivia provides them. If we confirm kernel retry loops, we'll prepare a targeted qprofile tweak (remove one optimization flag) and validate on a staging fleet within 30-45 minutes.

Irene Choi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
